BUILDING CONSTRUCTION — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #11
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: BUILDING CONSTRUCTION
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. Speaker
   B. Keyboard
   C. CPU
   D. Monitor

2. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun
   B. Ignore burnt cables
   C. Overload every socket
   D. Never touch live wires with wet hands

3. When learning Isometric Drawing, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Isometric Drawing.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Isometric Drawing.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Isometric Drawing.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Isometric Drawing.

4. When learning Introduction to Building Construction, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Introduction to Building Construction.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Introduction to Building Construction.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Introduction to Building Construction.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Introduction to Building Construction.

5. When learning Timbering 3.4 Foundation Walling 3.5 Ground Floors 4.0 Building Services 4.1 Plu, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Timbering 3.4 Foundation Walling 3.5 Ground Floors 4.0 Building Services 4.1 Plu.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Timbering 3.4 Foundation Walling 3.5 Ground Floors 4.0 Building Services 4.1 Plu.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Timbering 3.4 Foundation Walling 3.5 Ground Floors 4.0 Building Services 4.1 Plu.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Timbering 3.4 Foundation Walling 3.5 Ground Floors 4.0 Building Services 4.1 Plu.

6. When learning Computer Aided Drawing, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Computer Aided Drawing.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Computer Aided Drawing.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Computer Aided Drawing.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Computer Aided Drawing.

7. When learning Foundations, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Foundations.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Foundations.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Foundations.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Foundations.

8. When learning Site Preparation, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Site Preparation.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Site Preparation.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Site Preparation.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Site Preparation.

9. When learning Isometric Drawing 2.2 Computer Aided Drawing 3.0 Building Construction Processes, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Isometric Drawing 2.2 Computer Aided Drawing 3.0 Building Construction Processes.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Isometric Drawing 2.2 Computer Aided Drawing 3.0 Building Construction Processes.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Isometric Drawing 2.2 Computer Aided Drawing 3.0 Building Construction Processes.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Isometric Drawing 2.2 Computer Aided Drawing 3.0 Building Construction Processes.

10. When learning Introduction to Building Construction 1.2 Site Preparation 2.0 Related Drawing 2, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Introduction to Building Construction 1.2 Site Preparation 2.0 Related Drawing 2.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Introduction to Building Construction 1.2 Site Preparation 2.0 Related Drawing 2.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Introduction to Building Construction 1.2 Site Preparation 2.0 Related Drawing 2.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Introduction to Building Construction 1.2 Site Preparation 2.0 Related Drawing 2.

11. When learning Site Preparation 2.0 Related Drawing 2.1 Isometric Drawing 2.2 Computer Aided Dr, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Site Preparation 2.0 Related Drawing 2.1 Isometric Drawing 2.2 Computer Aided Dr.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Site Preparation 2.0 Related Drawing 2.1 Isometric Drawing 2.2 Computer Aided Dr.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Site Preparation 2.0 Related Drawing 2.1 Isometric Drawing 2.2 Computer Aided Dr.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Site Preparation 2.0 Related Drawing 2.1 Isometric Drawing 2.2 Computer Aided Dr.

12. When learning Timbering, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Timbering.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Timbering.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Timbering.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Timbering.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Computer Aided Drawing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Concreting 3.2 Foundations 3.3 Timbering 3.4 Foundation Walling 3.5 Ground Floor and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Concreting and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Foundations and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Concreting; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Foundations; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
